newsitem.title: UK: Reuters to return cash via special dividends.
newsitem.headline: Reuters to return cash via special dividends.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it proposed to return 613 million stg of cash to shareholders over three years through a bonus issue of a new class of special dividend shares.
Under the proposal and a share capital consolidation, shareholders will receive 19 ordinary shares and one special dividend share for every 20 shares held on October 8.

Each special dividend share will pay net dividends totalling 750p over the period against an average of the ordinary share price of 752p for the week to 9 September 1996, the international news and information organisation said.
Reuters said in a statement the share capital consolidation allows easy comparison with past performance of both earnings per share (EPS) and the ordinary share price.
The proposal is not expected to have any significant impact on EPS. The consolidation results in a five percent reduction in the number of ordinary shares in issue, the company said.

Reuters had already said it was looking at ways of returning surplus cash to shareholders. However, in the statement it said, "It was not possible to repeat the share repurchase structure which was adopted in 1993."
It said UK tax clearance was not available for such a structure this time.

Under the scheme, holders of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) will receive one special dividend American Depositary Share (ADS) and 19 new ADSs for every 20 ADSs held at the close of business on October 8, 1996.
Reuters said the payment will not diminish its high levels of investment for future growth.
"The company considers the proposal to be the best way of enabling shareholders to receive more cash, more efficiently, at a faster rate and on an equal basis," it said.

Reuters said comprehensive UK tax clearance had not been granted for the present proposal. "However, based on advice, the company believes this proposal avoids any tax disadvantage for existing shareholders in respect of their current holdings."
It said an on-market share repurchase was effectively ruled out because of the high proportion of holders in the U.S. and the board's objective of treating all shareholders equally.
SBC Warburg is independently offering to shareholders outside the U.S., Canada, Australia and Japan a special share dealing facility in the UK for the Special Dividend Shares, the company added.
Each special dividend share will pay six net dividends over the next three years of 125p each, giving total special dividends per share of 750p, the company said.

The first such special dividend will be paid on November 25, 1996 to holders of special dividend shares on the register on October 29. The second dividend will be payable on March 27, 1997, and, thereafter, dividends will be payable semi-annually on October 1 and March 31, up to and including March 31, 1999.
The dividends paid will be in addition to those declared on Reuters ordinary shares.
The proposal will be voted on at an extraordinary general meeting set for October 9.
Reuters has applied for the special dividend shares to be listed in the UK and the ADSs in the U.S. Trading in these shares is expected to begin on October 10.
The company said the proposal will result in Reuters having returned nearly one billion stg of surplus cash to shareholders in the 1990s, in addition to ordinary dividends.
